sentences.text: 2. Heard learned Counsel for the Applicants, learned APP for the State.
I have perused the records and considered the submissions advanced by the learned Counsel for the respective parties .
3. The aforesaid crime was registered pursuant to the FIR dated 24.12.2022 lodged by Dhiren Labhshankar Vyas.
The facts narrated in the FIR prima facie reveal that the applicant was in search of a flat at Kandivli.

One of the brokers informed him that Flat No. 507, B Wing, Meeth Niketan,
Thakur Complex, Kandivli, was for sale.
Accordingly, he met the applicant and her husband and other siblings.
They agreed to purchase the flat for Rs.1,20,00,000/-.
The first informant paid to the applicant Vishakha and her husband total amount of Rs.53,50,000/-.
The applicant and her husband subsequently failed to complete the transaction.

They repaid an amount of Rs.6,50,000/-
but refused to repay the balance amount.
Hence the FIR.

4. During the pendency of this application, the applicant filed her affidavit, wherein she has expressed her willingness to pay to the first informant total amount of Rs.53,50,000/- which was received in her account on various dates from 2019 onwards.
The applicant has given the schedule of payment in paragraph 3 of the affidavit.
The first informant, who is present before the court, is ready to receive the money SALGAONKAR 2 of 4 15 aba 528-23.doc
as per the schedule given in the affidavit.

Learned Counsel for the applicant has today handed over to the first informant a demand draft of Rs.5 lakhs.
5.

In view of the statement made by the applicant, and willingness shown to refund the amount of Rs.53,50,000/-, and since the parties are now exploring the possibility of amicable settlement, in my considered view, this is a fit case to exercise discretion under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
